|publisher=Instagram |access-date=11 October 2025 |date=July 2, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Vice">{{cite web | last=Usher | first=Tom | title=The Strange Allure of Extreme Alpha Male Influencers | |date=2026 |title=Theorizing the rise of internet food cults |journal=[[Food, Culture & Society]] |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=917–938|doi=10.1080/15528014.2025.2609250|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Rashid 2025">{{Cite magazine|last1=Rashid |first1=Hafiz|date=2026|title=Two Inept Male Trump Officials Talk About Nursing Babies|url=https://newrepublic.com/post/204151/two-male-trump-officials-nursing-babies|magazine=The New Republic|language=en-GB|archive-date=March 4, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260304072731/https://newrepublic.com/post/204151/two-male-trump-officials-nursing-babies|url-status=live|quote=Saladino, known for pushing pseudoscience like a carnivore diet and feeding raw milk to infants, didn’t broach the topic in his remarks.}}</ref> Saladino was formerly a leading advocate of the [[carnivore diet]],<ref name=":1" /><ref name="ABC">{{cite web |date=August 12, 2022 |title=Why the carnivore diet is popular right now |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-08-12/why-the-extreme-meat-carnivore-diet-is-so-popular-right-now/101317952 |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=ABC News}}</ref><ref name="CBS" /> a strict meat-only [[fad diet]] that lacks scientific evidence for its effectiveness.<ref name="Dennett">{{Cite web |last=Dennett |first=Carrie |date=May 2019 |title=Popular Diet Trends: Today's Fad Diets By Carrie Dennett, MPH, RDN, CD |url=https://www.todaysdietitian.com/newarchives/0519p12.shtml |access-date=February 4, 2020 |website=Today's Dietitian}}</ref> His 2020 book ''The Carnivore Code'' is described by ''[[The New Yorker]]'' as the closest thing the [[Paleo diet]] movement has to a manifesto. In it, Saladino described plants as "poison".<ref name="New Yorker">{{cite magazine |last=Singh |first=Manvir |date=September 25, 2023 |title=Is an All-Meat Diet What Nature Intended? |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2023/10/02/is-an-all-meat-diet-what-nature-intended |access-date=June 1, 2025 |magazine=The New Yorker}}</ref> Saladino later abandoned a strict carnivore diet citing serious side effects,<ref name="Bristol Post">{{cite web |last=Jenne |first=Ellen |date=January 12, 2025 |title=Man who followed 'carnivore diet' warns it's 'not great for most' |url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/health/expert-warns-of-carnivore-diet-9856007 |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=Bristol Live}}</ref><ref name="Guardian" /> pivoting to promoting a meat heavy diet that also includes fruit and honey.<ref name=":1" /> He also advocates for [[raw milk]],<ref name="CBS" /> despite the lack of evidence for any health benefits, and the [[Milk borne diseases|known serious health risks]] of drinking unpasteurized milk.<ref name="CBS" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Nutrition |first=Center for Food Safety and Applied |date=August 12, 2021 |title=Consumers – The Dangers of Raw Milk: Unpasteurized Milk Can Pose a Serious Health Risk |url=https://www.fda.gov/Food/ResourcesForYou/Consumers/ucm079516.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603133301/http://www.fda.gov/Food/ResourcesForYou/Consumers/ucm079516.htm |archive-date=June 3, 2009 |website=www.fda.gov}}</ref> 

He posts on [[social media]] under the name '''paulsaladinomd'''.<ref name="Newsweek" /> As of late 2025, his [[Instagram]] account has around 2.8 million followers<ref name="American Journal of Preventive Medicine">{{cite journal |last=Allem |first=Jon-Patrick |date=2024 |title=The Need for Research on the Wellness Industry's Impact on Health Decisions |journal=American Journal of Preventive Medicine |volume=67 |issue=4 |pages=627–630 |doi=10.1016/j.amepre.2024.05.010 |doi-access=free |pmid=38777206 }}</ref> and his [[TikTok]] channel over 700K followers.<ref name="CBS" /> He often appears shirtless in his videos.<ref name="ABC" /> He has said his Instagram and TikTok accounts have each been banned once.<ref name="Vice 2022">{{cite web |last=Merlan |first=Anna |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Why Are the Weirdest People Online Obsessed With Organ Meats? |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/why-are-the-weirdest-people-online-obsessed-with-organ-meats/ |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=VICE}}</ref>

Saladino is the founder{{efn|According to the company website, Saladino is the founder.<ref name=AboutH&S>{{cite web|accessdate=July 18, 2026 |url=https://heartandsoil.co/our-story/|title=Our Story|publisher=Heart & Soil|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260510021422/https://heartandsoil.co/our-story/|archivedate=May 10, 2026}}</ref>}} of '''Heart & Soil''',{{efn|The company name is styled with an ampersand, as "Heart & Soil".<ref name=CompanyInfo>{{cite web|accessdate=July 18, 2026 |url=https://heartandsoil.co/terms-of-service/ | date=July 1, 2024  |title=Terms of Service|publisher=Heart & Soil|quote=...Heart & Soil Supplements, LLC..., a Texas limited liability company.}}</ref>}}[[Austin, Texas]]-based company<ref name="LA Times" /> producing [[food supplements]].<ref name="American Journal of Preventive Medicine" /> Saladino co-owns it with fellow carnivore diet influencer Brian Johnson, known as [[Liver King]].<ref name="New Yorker" /> Heart & Soil sells bottles of encapsulated organ meat-based supplement products and [[liver pills]].<ref name="Vice 2022" /><ref name="GQ">{{cite web |last=Reiss |first=Sami |date=February 16, 2023 |title=A Unified Theory of the Trad Health Food Influencer |url=https://www.gq.com/story/a-unified-theory-of-the-trad-health-food-influencer |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=GQ}}</ref>

== Biography and education ==
Saladino earned a chemistry degree from the [[College of William and Mary]], followed by 6 years spent traveling in North America and New Zealand. He later became a [[physician assistant]] and later did training in [[cardiology]], gaining his [[Doctor of Medicine|MD]] from the [[University of Arizona]] in 2015, and completing his [[Residency (medicine)|residency]] at the [[University of Washington]] in 2019. Saladino has board certification in psychiatry and is a certified "[[Functional Medicine]]" practitioner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paul Saladino M.D. |url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/gb/contributors/paul-saladino-md |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=[[Psychology Today]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> As of 2022, his license to practice medicine in California was "delinquent" due to not paying fees.<ref name="Vice 2022" />

==Advocacy==
Prior to gaining mainstream attention, Saladino was [[vegan]].<ref name=":1" /> As an advocate of the strict meat only carnivore diet, Saladino argued that the diet could "cure everything ranging from depression to autoimmune conditions", and claimed that the diet cured his anxiety and eczema.<ref name=":1" /> He transitioned away from a strict carnivore diet by 2020 by adding [[carbohydrate]]s to his diet, including fruit and honey.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|author=Kurutz, Steven|date=2024|title=Meet the Men Who Eat Meat (and Only Meat)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/04/30/style/meet-the-men-who-eat-meat-and-only-meat.html|website=The New York Times|language=en-GB|archive-date=June 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250613154724/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/04/30/style/meet-the-men-who-eat-meat-and-only-meat.html|url-status=live}}</ref> While on the carnivore diet, Saladino reported experiencing [[sleep disturbances]], [[heart palpitations]], [[muscle cramps]], and a drop in [[testosterone]] levels.<ref name="Bristol Post" /><ref name="Guardian">{{cite news|title='Plants are trying to kill you': why carnivore influencers claim we should eat only meat|first=Niloufar|last=Haidari|date=September 13, 2024|access-date=May 18, 2026|work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/food/2024/sep/12/carnivore-diet-meat-plants|quote=Saladino said the diet was causing him sleep issues, muscle pain and low testosterone.}}</ref> He said: "I started to think, maybe long-term [[ketosis]] is not great for me" and "probably not a great thing for most humans".<ref name="Bristol Post" /><ref name="Surrey Live">{{cite web |last=Jenne |first=Ellen |date=January 12, 2025 |title=Health expert abandons carnivore diet after suffering heart issues |url=https://www.getsurrey.co.uk/news/health/health-expert-abandons-carnivore-diet-30756276 |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=Surrey Live}}</ref><ref name="Wales">{{cite web |last=Jenne |first=Ellen |date=May 8, 2024 |title=Alarming side effects of 'carnivore diet' as man left with heart issues |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/health/expert-warns-of-carnivore-diet-29130977 |access-date=June 1, 2025 |website=Wales Online}}</ref> Saladino's content often features him [[vlogging]] and presenting lifestyle advice and his personal routine, in scenarios varying from supermarket trips to surfing on his Costa Rican estate.<ref name=":1" />

He promotes the consumption of animal organs, claiming they help [[Immunity (medical)|immunity]], [[gut health]], [[weight loss]] and bone strength.<ref name="LA Times">{{cite web | last=Vankin | first=Deborah | title='Who is buying this?!' Has Erewhon's Raw Animal Smoothie taken L.A. health food too far? | website=Los Angeles Times | date=July 18, 2024 | url=https://www.latimes.com/lifestyle/story/2024-07-18/erewhon-smoothie-raw-animal-organs-safe | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref> Saladino has urged his followers to use a bidet instead of [[toilet paper]], claiming that toilet paper is "filled with [[hormone]] disrupting compounds" and that he avoids contact with them to "protect" his "hormonal health".<ref name="j917">{{cite journal | last=Maddalena | first=Kate | title="Smart drugs," Gender, and the Rhetorical Turning | journal=Poroi | volume=18 | issue=1 | date=December 11, 2024 | issn=2151-2957 | doi=10.17077/2151-2957.33739 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

According to [[Vice.com]], during the [[Coronavirus pandemic]], he was increasingly dismissive of the efficacy of [[vaccines]] contrary to mainstream scientific opinion, although saying they "may help avoid some severe [[COVID-19]] complications." However, he asserted that "[[metabolic]] health" and "[[natural immunity]]" are more effective, also against medical consensus.<ref name="Vice 2022"/>

He described in a 2022 [[viral video]] a hygiene regime that eschews the use of [[shampoo]], [[soap]], [[deodorant]] and [[toothpaste]] in favor of simply water.<ref name="Newsweek"/>

He posted a video to his [[Twitter|X.com]] account in May 2024 that promoted feeding "raw dairy" to infants. The post received over 90,000 views and sparked strong backlash before it was removed the following day.<ref name="CBS">{{cite web | last=Doan | first=Laura | title=Influencers promote raw milk despite FDA health warnings as bird flu spreads in dairy cows | website=CBS News | date=May 13, 2024 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bird-flu-raw-milk-influencers-fda-warning/ | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref>

He conducted an interview with [[United States Secretary of Health and Human Services|United States secretary of health and human services]] [[Robert F. Kennedy Jr]] in the [[White House]] in May 2025. In the promotional video, the two men are shown drinking shots of raw milk mixed with [[glyphosate]]-free [[honey]].<ref name="The Cut">{{cite web | last=Dickson | first=E.J. | title=RFK Jr. Did Raw-Milk Shooters in the White House | website=The Cut | date=May 30, 2025 | url=https://www.thecut.com/article/rfk-jr-celebrated-his-maha-report-with-raw-milk-shooters.html | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Rolling Stone">{{cite magazine | last=Madarang | first=Charisma | title=Why Are Health Influencers Drinking Raw Milk and Honey Shots at the White House? | magazine=Rolling Stone | date=May 28, 2025 | url=https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/raw-milk-honey-maha-report-white-house-influencers-1235349031/ | access-date=June 1, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250528051457/https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/raw-milk-honey-maha-report-white-house-influencers-1235349031/ |archive-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref><ref name="DB">{{cite web | last=Kimmins | first=Leigh | title=RFK Jr. Chugs Raw Milk With Crackpot Doc at White House | website=The Daily Beast | date=May 30, 2025 | url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/rfk-jr-chugs-raw-milk-with-crackpot-doc-at-white-house/ | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref>

Saladino is known for his [[Seed oil misinformation|opposition to seed oils]].<ref>{{cite magazine|author1-first= Audrey| author1-last= Carleton| date	= March 22, 2022| title	= The newest Bitcoin diet trend is hating 'seed oils'| language= en| magazine	= Vice| department= Motherboard| url= https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-newest-bitcoin-diet-trend-is-hating-seed-oils/| access-date= August 27, 2024| archive-url	= https://web.archive.org/web/20220322133939/https://www.vice.com/en/article/v7djay/the-newest-bitcoin-diet-trend-is-hating-seed-oils| archive-date= March 22, 2022| url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|author=Willmoth, Hatty|date=2026|title=Seed oils vs butter: Here's what's actually healthier, according to doctors|url=https://www.sciencefocus.com/the-human-body/seed-oils-vs-butter-healthier|website=BBC Science Focus|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Collaborations==
Saladino describes himself as an "adventure buddy" of another carnivore diet influencer, [[Anthony Gustin]], founder of online food store [[Perfect Keto]]. The pair visited the [[Hadza people]] of [[Tanzania]] in 2022, promoting them as a dietary model; Saladino said "The Hadza are the closest thing we have to a time machine." According to science writer Dorsa Amir, "the idea that the 'correct' diet is an ancient one is also the backbone of fads like the [[paleo diet]], [and] Saladino's carnivore diet."<ref name="j247">{{cite web | last=Amir | first=Dorsa | title=A Viral Twitter Thread Reawakens the Dark History of Anthropology | website=Nautilus | date=April 22, 2022 | url=https://nautil.us/a-viral-twitter-thread-reawakens-the-dark-history-of-anthropology-238468/ | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref> Saladino is the founder of '''Heart & Soil''', an [[Austin, Texas]]-based company<ref name="LA Times" /> producing [[food supplements]].<ref name="American Journal of Preventive Medicine" /> Saladino co-owns it with fellow carnivore diet influencer Brian Johnson, known as [[Liver King]].<ref name="New Yorker" /> Heart & Soil sells bottles of encapsulated organ meat-based supplement products and [[liver pills]].<ref name="Vice 2022" /><ref name="GQ" />

He collaborated with [[California]] luxury grocery store [[Erewhon (store)|Erewhon]] in 2023 on the store's Raw Animal-Based Smoothie, which mixes [[kefir]] (fermented milk), along with other ingredients, with beef organs and "[[Immunomilk]]" (a product made of freeze-dried cow's [[colostrum]]).<ref name="LA Times"/> The raw milk was supplied by California-based [[Raw Farms]], until it switched to [[pasteurization]] after tests of its milk turned up positive for [[H5N1]] [[influenza A virus]].<ref name="Bus Ins">{{cite web |last=Brueck |first=Hilary |title=The man behind one of the buzziest raw milk farms explains why they are going pasteurized |website=Business Insider |date=December 5, 2024 |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/raw-milk-in-california-being-pasteurized-bird-flu-sweeps-state-2024-12 |access-date=June 1, 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205182650/https://www.businessinsider.com/raw-milk-in-california-being-pasteurized-bird-flu-sweeps-state-2024-12 |archive-date=December 5, 2024}}</ref> Consuming raw animal meat poses a risk of bacterial infection.<ref name="LA Times" />

==Influence and reception==

Saladino influenced [[Low-carbohydrate diet|low carb diet]] entrepreneur [[Dave Asprey]] and celebrity [[Heidi Montag]] to begin the carnivore diet.<ref name="Vice 2022"/> Saladino appeared on [[Joe Rogan]]'s [[The Joe Rogan Experience|podcast]] in 2020,<ref name="Vice"/><ref name="Newsweek">{{cite web | last=Beresford | first=Jack | title=Internet Retches at Man Who Doesn't Use Shampoo or Toothpaste: 'Rancid' | website=Newsweek | date=June 22, 2022 | url=https://www.newsweek.com/man-does-not-use-shampoo-soap-deodorant-toothpaste-rancid-tiktok-1718108 | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref><ref name="GQ 2021">{{cite web | last=Zaleski | first=Andrew | title=Seed Oil Is the Latest Thing We're Being Told to Eliminate from Our Diets—Here's Why | website=GQ | date=October 14, 2021 | url=https://www.gq.com/story/seed-oil-health | access-date=June 1, 2025}}</ref> which greatly expanded his audience and profile.<ref name="Vice 2022"/> Alexei Anisin, writing in the journal ''[[Food, Culture & Society]]'', has said that Saladino's medical background and "pseudo-academic" style has given his content an air of perceived "scientific authority", while Saladino himself remains personally accessible to viewers, which, in combination with the high production quality of his videos, has led his viewers to trust him.<ref name=":1" /> Hafiz Rashid of ''[[The New Republic]]'' has described Saladino as an "infamous pseudoscience health influencer".<ref name="Rashid 2025"/>  

Science communicator [[Joseph A. Schwarcz]], in reference to a claim by Saladino that "eating a serving of McDonald’s fries is equivalent to smoking a pack of 25 cigarettes", has said: "Fearmongering has become an industry, and Saladino is a head honcho in this arena. The usual technique [for Saladino] is to pick a scientific study that finds some risk and then exaggerate it without taking into account type and extent of exposure." Schwarcz says that Saladino "thinks that lamb testicles and raw liver are healthy, and [[cruciferous vegetables]] like [[broccoli]], [[Brussels sprout|Brussels sprouts]], [[chard]] and [[kale]] are 'bulls–t.' These, Saladino says, should be avoided because 'once chewed they produce [[sulforaphane]], which is toxic to humans.' Actually, sulforaphane has been shown to be an [[anti-carcinogen]]".<ref name="f918">{{cite web |last=Schwarcz |first=Joe |date=May 10, 2024 |title=No, Eating French Fries is Not the Same as Smoking Cigarettes |url=https://www.mcgill.ca/oss/article/critical-thinking-health-and-nutrition-pseudoscience/no-eating-french-fries-not-same-smoking-cigarettes |access-date=June 1, 2025 |publisher=[[Office for Science and Society]]}}</ref>
